title: King of Thorn
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: As the Medusa virus turns its victims to stone, twin sisters Kasumi and Shizuku are separated when only Kasumi is chosen as one of 160 people placed in cold sleep until a cure is found (TOKYOPOP blurb via AniList; MangaUpdates). She wakes in a facility overgrown with thorns and full of people-eating monsters, and a small group of survivors, including the 'bad-boy' Marco Owens, investigates what happened (MangaUpdates; ANN review of volumes 1-3).
life_message: Holding on to love and courage under impossible odds is what keeps people human.

content.note: 'People-eating monsters' and 'plenty enough graphic content to justify its Older Teens rating' (ANN); Body Horror (AniList); most survivors die early (MangaUpdates blurb).
'Horror-laced', 'truly nerve-wracking' (ANN); petrifying virus, monsters (blurbs); Survival, Post-Apocalyptic (AniList).
ANN: no actual nudity and little fan service.
Terminal illness and separation of twins (blurbs); Tragedy (AniList).

dominant: Survival horror; sisterly love; corporate science gone wrong

frames.aligns: Kasumi's love for Shizuku and the survivors' mutual aid.
frames.concerns: Graphic monster deaths; selection of who lives raises dignity questions.

frames.aligns: Hope and loyalty in a fallen world.
Human hubris of the Venus Gate Corporation exposed.
Critique of corporate control over who gets saved.
Impermanence and attachment explored through the twins.
Female lead; critique of unequal access to a cure.
Science fiction mystery solved by investigation.
Nature reclaims the facility in thorns.
Self-preservation and distrust of a corporation.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Survivors distrust each other (ANN) but no honor code.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Corporate plan imposed, then breaks down (blurbs).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Twin bond alongside a group of strangers (blurbs).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Science, cold sleep and corporate research (blurbs).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival is the whole plot (AniList Survival).

folkways.japan: Fits a Japanese seinen survival tradition where the group's cooperation under crisis is tested.

delivery.evidence: ANN discusses tension and characters, not message (to verify).
delivery.note: Themes come through the survival plot rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Kasumi and the survivors draw sympathy; the Venus Gate Corporation's intentions are questioned; ending not in opened sources.
to_verify: English license is partial or lapsed (TOKYOPOP; MangaUpdates lists licensed: false, out of print).
ANN review covers volumes 1-3; later violence not checked.
An animated film exists (MangaUpdates 'Adapted to Movie'); sources here cover the manga.
